disaster.name: Hurricane Isaias October 2026
disaster.overview:
Status: Response Phase / VOLUNTEER OPPORTUNITIES


READY TO SERVE? Here is your Connection...

Disaster response takes all of us. From feeding families and clearing debris to tree removal, cleanup, and providing essential resources, trusted Response Partners are stepping up to serve communities in need. Here are the steps:


  1. Explore the map and partner list below to find trusted organizations actively serving.
  2. Discover your chosen organization's next steps for individuals and groups ready to volunteer.
  3. Finally - sign up, show up and SERVE!
  4. Need help - CONTACT Serve Source.


((First - Scroll to the Response map below))


Event Update

Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, at approximately 8:30 PM CDT Friday, October 9, as a Category 2 hurricane with maximum sustained winds near 105 mph. It has since weakened into a post-tropical cyclone and moved inland through Alabama into Tennessee.


The hurricane threat along the northern Gulf Coast has ended, but response and recovery are underway across communities affected by damaging winds, power outages, flooding, debris, and damage to homes, churches, and community facilities.


Serve Source is connecting churches, disaster-response ministries, and local leaders as verified needs become clear. Visit the response map to follow partner activity, share available resources, request help, and identify coordinated opportunities to serve. Everyone can do something—pray, give, share resources, or join a verified response effort.

Current Situation

Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, on October 9 as a Category 2 hurricane. The National Hurricane Center discontinued advisories on October 10 after Isaias weakened to a post-tropical cyclone over Alabama.


This is now a recovery event. The most immediate concerns are damaged homes, fallen trees, large debris volumes, road and utility hazards, household needs, and helping affected communities begin the long path toward recovery.

Recovery-Phase Hazards

  • Localized flooding, standing water, and hazardous road conditions
  • Downed trees, damaged structures, and blocked access routes
  • Downed or damaged power lines; treat all lines as energized
  • Scattered power outages and utility-restoration activity
  • Lingering rain and gusty winds across portions of Tennessee and the southern Appalachians
  • Dangerous coastal conditions may continue in some areas; follow local beach and emergency-management guidance

Residents should continue to follow instructions from local emergency management and the National Weather Service. Do not drive through floodwater, around barricades, or into areas with downed lines or unstable trees.

Areas of Initial Response Focus

Serve Source is monitoring verified impacts and partner activity across:

  • Florida Panhandle: Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa, Walton, Bay, Holmes, and Washington Counties
  • Alabama: Baldwin, Mobile, Escambia, Conecuh, Covington, and other affected inland communities
  • Coastal Mississippi and southeastern Louisiana: continuing local monitoring for rain, coastal, and recovery-related impacts
  • Tennessee and the southern Appalachians: lingering rain and wind impacts as the post-tropical system moves northeast

This list reflects the areas of greatest expected or reported impact and may change as local damage assessments continue.

Partner Preparedness & Coordination

Serve Source has moved from storm monitoring to assessment and response coordination.


Partners shown on the Serve Source response map are reporting activities that may include:

  • Damage assessments and verified-needs reporting
  • Emergency meals, food distribution, water, and essential supplies
  • Resource and donation coordination
  • Tree and debris removal
  • Roof tarping and temporary weatherproofing
  • Flood cleanup and muck-out assistance where needed
  • Mobile shower, laundry, and volunteer-support services
  • Church, volunteer, and housing coordination


Churches and response organizations are encouraged to:

  • Update their Serve Source profile and response capabilities.
  • Submit verified local needs, damage reports, and available resources.
  • Coordinate with local emergency management before opening facilities or receiving volunteers.
  • Use the response map to connect with churches and organizations already serving nearby.
  • Avoid self-deployment. Wait for a verified request, local invitation, or coordinated deployment opportunity.
  • Share prayer needs and encourage affected leaders through the Serve Source event page.
  • If your church has been affected, needs assistance, has available resources, or is ready to serve, please update the Hurricane Isaias Active Event page so partners can respond in coordination.

Partner Response Efforts & Church Locations

Recovery is underway across the Florida Panhandle and southern Alabama. State, local, nonprofit, and faith-based partners are supporting feeding, supply distribution, damage assessment, debris removal, roof tarping, and survivor referrals. Florida has operated distribution points in impacted Panhandle counties, while local recovery coordination continues to expand. Executive Office of the Governor


The following partner and church response locations are currently shown on the Serve Source Hurricane Isaias Active Event Map. Availability, service areas, and volunteer needs may change quickly—please open each response card or contact the organization before traveling.


Active Partner Response

  • BRACE (Be Ready Alliance Coordinating for Emergencies) — coordinating local, national, and long-term recovery partners serving Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties.
  • Mercy Chefs — meal-response support in Pensacola through Transformation Church.
  • Convoy of Hope — relief-supply and logistics support at Pace Assembly Ministries in Pace.
  • Hope Force International — roof tarping and muck-out support through the Pensacola Dream Center.
  • God’s Pit Crew — tree work, tarping, and debris removal staged through Pace Assembly.
  • Samaritan’s Purse — cleanup, tree work, and tarping assistance at church-host sites in Pace and Brewton.
  • Eight Days of Hope — feeding and cleanup support in Navarre, with a planned Pensacola response location.
  • Operation Blessing — meals, resources, and damage-assessment support in Pensacola.
  • Here to Serve — meal support through Christ Methodist Church in Milton.
  • Minuteman Disaster Response and Renewed Ground Disaster Relief — debris-removal and recovery support.
  • Operation Airdrop — aviation and logistics support from Gulf Shores.
  • Texas Baptist Disaster Relief — cleanup, tree work, and tarping assistance at church-host sites in Milton and Pensacola
  • On Mission Network — cleanup, tree work, and tarping assistance at church-host sites in Milton and Pensacola


Churches Serving as Response or Host Locations

  • First Baptist Church of Brewton — Brewton, AL, hosting Samaritan’s Purse
  • City Hope Church — Daphne, AL
  • Worship on the Water Ministry Center — Orange Beach, AL
  • Oak Park Church — supporting meal, shower, and laundry services through Pace Assembly


Response details, locations, dates, and volunteer opportunities may change as assessments continue. Visit the Serve Source response map below to connect directly with responding organizations, submit a verified need, share a resource, or find an opportunity to serve.


Not yet connected in Serve Source? REGISTER YOU CHURCH or ORGANIZATION


Potential response activities following landfall may include emergency feeding, distribution of essential supplies, debris removal, roof tarping, flood cleanup, temporary shelter assistance, and support for families experiencing displacement or damage to their homes.


Deployment opportunities and specific resource requests will be shared as needs are verified and coordination with local leaders is established.


Serve Source will continue monitoring official forecasts, emerging disaster impacts, and partner response activities to help churches and disaster response organizations connect, communicate, and coordinate effectively.

Need Cleanup Help?

Residents in Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties who need help with storm cleanup can contact Crisis Cleanup to be connected with volunteer organizations that may be able to assist.

  • Roof tarping
  • Fallen-tree removal
  • Debris cleanup
  • Mucking out flooded homes
  • Other storm-cleanup needs


Call Crisis Cleanup: 1-800-451-1954

BRACE is coordinating with national disaster-relief organizations, local partners, and Long-Term Recovery Groups to help connect residents with available assistance. Assistance is dependent on volunteer capacity, safety conditions, and the needs reported. 


Weather Maps & Official Updates

Serve Source is compiling information for this event from the following official and trusted sources:

  • National Hurricane Center — Hurricane Isaias Advisory Archive
  • National Hurricane Center — Forecast, Rainfall, Surge, and Wind Graphics
  • National Weather Service — Mobile/Pensacola

Conditions, road access, local protective actions, and response opportunities may change quickly. Follow local emergency management and National Weather Service offices for the latest official information.

organization.name: BRACE
organization.description: Be Ready Alliance Coordinating for Emergencies (BRACE) is Northwest Florida’s leading disaster preparedness, response, and recovery organization. Serving Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties, BRACE strengthens community resilience by coordinating more than 500 partner organizations, training volunteers through Citizen Corps, CERT, and Fire Corps programs, and managing both county Long-Term Recovery Groups. As the fiscal agent and ESF-15 (Volunteers & Donations) lead for Escambia County and Santa Rosa County Emergency Management, BRACE mobilizes resources and volunteers before, during, and after disasters to meet the needs of impacted families. The organization also leads public education efforts such as the StormWise Disaster Preparedness Workshop, Disaster Services Expo, Faith Leader Emergency Summit, Disaster Services RoundTable, and Storms & Stars Soiree, which connect residents, businesses, and community leaders with the tools and training to prepare, mitigate, and recover from disasters. Through collaboration, compassion, and innovation, BRACE helps Northwest Florida build safer, stronger, and more resilient communities.

responses.narrative:
Jubilee Church in Pensacola is serving as a community disaster relief hub following Hurricane Isaias, partnering with United Cajun Navy and Mercy Chefs to provide practical assistance to affected families. The church is hosting the distribution of emergency supplies, including water, food, diapers, hygiene products, cleaning supplies, and other household essentials. Mercy Chefs is also providing hot meals at the church.

In addition to supply distribution and feeding, Jubilee Church is supporting disaster response volunteers and serving as a staging location for United Cajun Navy teams assisting with storm cleanup and debris removal. The church is also helping connect residents with available assistance by receiving requests for food, temporary housing, home repairs, tree removal, transportation, prayer, and other recovery needs, then coordinating referrals and follow-up with available response partners.

Jubilee Church is helping connect local community needs with responding organizations, volunteers, and resources as recovery efforts continue.

Destiny Worship Center in Navarre, Florida, is supporting Hurricane Isaias disaster relief efforts by partnering with Eight Days of Hope to provide free hot meals to residents impacted by the storm. The church is hosting a mass-feeding operation at its Navarre campus, serving as a community relief location where families experiencing power outages and other storm-related hardships can receive freshly prepared meals.

Beginning October 11, Eight Days of Hope deployed its emergency feeding ministry to the church, distributing meals to affected residents and coordinating local volunteers to support the operation. The feeding ministry plans to continue serving the community as needs persist and electrical service is restored.

Through this partnership, Destiny Worship Center is helping connect local residents with practical disaster assistance while providing a church-based location for a national Christian disaster relief organization to serve the community.

organization.name: Eight Days of Hope
organization.description: Eight Days of Hope serves as the hands and feet of Christ – providing light in the face of darkness, restoration in the face of destruction. We are a national organization that responds to disasters across the country, helping to rebuild homes, communities, and lives.

responses.narrative:
Our Mass Feeding team is deploying to serve the Navarre, FL, community impacted by Hurricane Isaias! Currently, there are about 100,000 people without power in this area. We are humbled to bring hope and help to this community - serving thousands of meals and reminding people that they are not alone in this heartbreaking time! 

We will be setting up to serve free, hot meals beginning at Noon on Sunday, October 11, at Destiny Worship Center – Navarre Campus (8860 Navarre Pkwy, Navarre, FL, 32566) and will continue serving until the need subsides and power is restored across the community. 

Pray: Please pray for those impacted by Isaias, for our Mass Feeding team, and for every person we have the opportunity to serve. Pray that the love of Jesus would be evident through every meal and every conversation. 

Serve: Currently, we are only accepting local volunteers. If you are in this area and would like to serve, please email feeding@eightdaysofhope.com. Once safe lodging accommodations have been secured, we may open this outreach to additional volunteers! 

Give: Every meal we serve is made possible through your generosity. To support our Mass Feeding efforts in Navarre, text GIVE to 86373 or visit eightdaysofhope.com. 

A meal may seem simple, but in the aftermath of a disaster, it can be a meaningful reminder that someone cares. Please pray that God would use every meal and every interaction to make an eternal impact!  See our Rapid Response Team (Oct 15-31).

organization.name: Worship on the Water
organization.description:
Starting in 2011, Worship on the Water was birthed out of a desire to BE the Church, not just build another one. With a burden to reach the lost, hurting, traveling, or wondering... Worship on the Water began meeting people at the world-famous Flora-Bama. Known for it’s iconic music environments, it’s drinks, and a place where all are welcome, Flora-Bama opened it’s doors and has partnered with Worship on the Water in a way that we hope to duplicate all over the Gulf Coast.

Since first opening the doors to turn a tent stage into a place of worship every Sunday, tens of thousands of locals and tourists alike have visited this special place. Thousands have made decisions to commit their lives to Christ, and even followed that up with being baptized just steps away in the Gulf.

Our focus is simple: raise up uncommon people, to carry uncommon faith into uncommon places. We hope you’ll join us!
